def make(root, rel, data=b"x"):
    path = root / rel
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_bytes(data)
    return path


def test_select_jobs_takes_documents_scans_first(tmp_path):
    make(tmp_path, "b/doc.pdf")
    make(tmp_path, "a/scan.jpg")
    make(tmp_path, "a/notes.csv")
    make(tmp_path, "a/.hidden.png")
    jobs = select_jobs(tmp_path, None, False, None)
    assert [j.rel for j in jobs] == ["a/scan.jpg", "b/doc.pdf"]
    assert [j.rel for j in select_jobs(tmp_path, None, True, None)] == ["a/scan.jpg"]
    assert [j.rel for j in select_jobs(tmp_path, "doc", False, None)] == ["b/doc.pdf"]


def test_changed_file_is_read_again(tmp_path):
    root, out = tmp_path / "portal", tmp_path / "out"
    make(root, "x/scan.jpg", b"v1")
    job = select_jobs(root, None, False, None)[0]
    (out / job.folder).mkdir(parents=True)
    (out / job.folder / "meta.json").write_text(json.dumps({"status": "ok", "sha256": job.sha256}))
    assert is_done(job, out)
    make(root, "x/scan.jpg", b"v2")
    changed = select_jobs(root, None, False, None)[0]
    assert not is_done(changed, out)  # new checksum, new folder


def test_failed_read_is_not_done(tmp_path):
    root, out = tmp_path / "portal", tmp_path / "out"
    make(root, "x/scan.jpg")
    job = select_jobs(root, None, False, None)[0]
    (out / job.folder).mkdir(parents=True)
    (out / job.folder / "meta.json").write_text(json.dumps({"status": "error", "sha256": job.sha256}))
    assert not is_done(job, out)


def test_clean_drops_image_bytes_and_keeps_block_types():
    message = AssistantMessage(content=[TextBlock(text="hi")], model="m")
    cleaned = _clean({"msg": message, "image": {"data": "A" * 5000}})
    assert cleaned["msg"]["_type"] == "AssistantMessage"
    assert cleaned["msg"]["content"][0]["_type"] == "TextBlock"
    assert "left out" in cleaned["image"]["data"]


def test_safety_blocks_are_not_retried():
    assert _not_retryable("API Error: Sonnet 5.5's safeguards flagged this message")
    assert not _not_retryable("ProcessError: exit code 1")


def test_schema_requires_every_field():
    # Structured output needs every property listed as required, at every level
    def check(node):
        if isinstance(node, dict):
            if node.get("type") == "object" and "properties" in node:
                assert set(node["required"]) == set(node["properties"]), node["required"]
                assert node.get("additionalProperties") is False
            for value in node.values():
                check(value)
        elif isinstance(node, list):

# Findings from the discovery run (21 Nov)

283 of 289 documents were read with `claude-sonnet-5-5`. 6 large scans were skipped (see README, "Not read yet"). The run compared the reader's output with `goods_receipts.csv` and `purchase_orders_2025H2-2026.csv`.

## What the paper says vs SAP: 5 categories

| # | Category | Cases | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Booked quantity ≠ paper** | 1 | `WZ-261116-473` art book: paper 8,000 (80.000 crossed out), SAP received 80,000, PO 8,000 (S1). The other 68 booked delivery notes match exactly. |
| 2 | **Arrived but not booked** | 3 | `DN-261120-726`: **28,000 GH6 game cards received 21 Nov** (the P2 air shipment). `WZ-261120-732`: 20,000 GH6 sleeves received 21 Nov. `DN-261119-197`: 10,500 GH5 cards from Boise (5,000 + 5,500). None is in SAP yet. |
| 3 | **Supplier terms ≠ SAP** | ~50 | **Price:** Hwaseong 5.51, 5.56 and 5.62 vs SAP 5.40 (P9). Boise 4500318533 at 6.29 vs SAP 6.11 (new). **Date:** Hwaseong 4500318636 confirms 9 Jun, SAP says 26 May (P10). **Incoterm:** about 40 Boise confirmations say EXW Boise, SAP says DDP Hamburg (P13), and 7 of them also say "freight prepaid by Seller". |
| 4 | **Wrong or different product** | 11 | Karton prints the GH6 sleeve to rev. C (10 confirmations, P3). **New:** `WZ-261120-732` has the handwritten remark "1 Pal. = GH5 Sleeves!", so one of its 10 pallets is the wrong sleeve. |
| 5 | **Status and quality claims** | 7 | Pune claims "approved for serial supply" in 6 confirmations, while SAP has it as conditional (P16). Inspection report 5000413063: lot **failed**, 9 of 125 defective, accept number 3 (S2). |

**Lesson:** SAP is right line by line almost everywhere: 0 quantity mismatches across 436 confirmation values, and 68 of 69 delivery notes match. The problems are rare but critical bookings (category 1), **timing**, where paper is ahead of SAP (category 2), and terms the supplier sets differently (category 3).

## Reader errors: 4 kinds

| Error | Cases | Fix (in the join, no new run needed) |
|---|---|---|
| Thousands dot misread: `5.000` gives `number` 5, mostly on Chinese and English notes | 11 | Re-parse from the raw `value`: a dot or comma followed by exactly 3 digits is a thousands separator. Check against the PO quantity. |
| Signatures and receiving stamps listed as `corrections` | 24 of 25 | Count only corrections with an `original` value |
| Supplier part numbers (`PR-…`) instead of `CMP-…` | 30 PackRight lines | Map with contract Annex C (already read) |
| SDK 1 MB message limit on large files | 6 | Skipped. Raise `max_buffer_size` later. |

Field names stayed stable: only 13 values used `other` (downtime dates, approval limits).

## Not in the linker yet

These results are only in `data/store/image_recognizer/`. Loading them into the linker as claims is the next step (M3: join adapter).

# Fields that count whole things. Only these get the thousands rule; a price such as
# '1.520' must stay 1.52.
COUNT_FIELDS = {
    "quantity_ordered",
    "quantity_confirmed",
    "quantity_shipped",
    "quantity_delivered",
    "quantity_received",
    "quantity_balance",
    "quantity_rejected",
    "lot_size",

}


def count_number(field: str, raw, model_number: float | None) -> float | None:
    """
    The number a count means, from the raw text as written.

    A count can't be fractional, so a group of three digits after a dot, comma or space is a
    thousands group, whatever the document's language: '19.000', '14.600', '8 000', '48,000'.
    Readers get this wrong on some documents; the raw text is the evidence, so it decides.
    Other fields keep the reader's number.
    """
    if field not in COUNT_FIELDS:
        return model_number
    text = clean(raw)
    if text is None:
        return model_number
    match = _GROUPED_THOUSANDS.search(text)
    if match and match.group(0) == re.search(r"[\d.,  ]+", text).group(0).strip():
        return float(re.sub(r"\D", "", match.group(0)))
    return model_number

input.content:
"""
Readings (M3): what the image recognizer read from each document, as linker records.

One 'reading' record per document (keys from the references inside it) and one 'doc_line' record
per line on it (part and values). Fixes for known reader errors are applied here, on load:
- counts are re-parsed from the raw text ('19.000' is 19000, see normalize.count_number)
- corrections are derived from the values (crossed out or handwritten), not taken from the
  reader's own list, which mostly holds signatures and stamps
- supplier part numbers are mapped to the buyer's (map_supplier_part_numbers)

The raw text of every value is kept next to the number, so nothing the reader saw is lost.
"""

import hashlib
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from verifier.linker.normalize import clean, count_number
from verifier.linker.records import make_record

REFERENCE_KEYS = {
    "po_number": "po_numbers",
    "delivery_note": "delivery_note",
    "air_waybill": "reference",
    "container": "reference",
    "batch": "batch",
    "goods_receipt": "batch",  # a goods receipt number is the batch number
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReadingSource:
    """Where a reading came from, shaped like a discovered Source for make_record."""

    path: str
    sha256: str


def _references(verdict: dict) -> dict:
    keys: dict = {"po_numbers": []}
    for ref in verdict.get("references") or []:
        column = REFERENCE_KEYS.get(ref.get("type"))
        value = clean(ref.get("value"))
        if column is None or value is None:
            continue
        if column == "po_numbers":
            if value not in keys["po_numbers"]:
                keys["po_numbers"].append(value)
        else:
            keys.setdefault(column, value)
    return keys


def _value(raw: dict) -> dict:
    field = raw.get("field")
    return {
        "field": field if field != "other" else f"other:{raw.get('field_label') or '?'}",
        "raw": raw.get("value"),
        "number": count_number(field, raw.get("value"), raw.get("number")),
        "unit": raw.get("unit"),
        "written": raw.get("written"),
        "crossed_out": bool(raw.get("crossed_out")),
        "legible": raw.get("legible"),
    }


def final_values(values: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """Per field, the value that stands: not crossed out; handwritten beats printed."""
    standing: dict = {}
    for value in values:
        if value["crossed_out"]:
            continue
        current = standing.get(value["field"])
        if current is None or (value["written"] == "handwritten" and current["written"] != "handwritten"):
            standing[value["field"]] = value
    return standing


def load_readings(readings_dir: Path, current_sha: dict[str, str]) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict]]:
    """
    Records from every successful reading. Returns (records, source rows for the summary).

    current_sha maps each portal path to its current checksum, so a reading of an older version
    of a file is still loaded but marked (attrs.read_sha256 differs), never silently trusted.
    """
    records, rows = [], []
    for meta_path in sorted(readings_dir.glob("*/meta.json")):
        verdict_path = meta_path.parent / "verdict.json"
        try:
            meta = json.loads(meta_path.read_text())
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if meta.get("status") != "ok" or not verdict_path.exists():
            continue
        verdict = json.loads(verdict_path.read_text())
        doc_path = meta["path"]
        source = ReadingSource(
            f"{readings_dir.name}/{meta_path.parent.name}/verdict.json",
            hashlib.sha256(verdict_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        )
        keys = _references(verdict)
        lines = [[_value(v) for v in line.get("values") or []] for line in verdict.get("lines") or []]
        all_values = [v for line in lines for v in line]
        received = next((v["raw"] for v in all_values if v["field"] == "date_received"), None)
        verdict_block = verdict.get("verdict") or {}
        attrs = {
            "doc_type": verdict.get("document_type"),
            "document_number": verdict.get("document_number"),
            "document_date": verdict.get("document_date"),
            "issuer": verdict.get("issuer"),
            "date_received": received,
            "status": verdict_block.get("status"),
            "confidence": verdict_block.get("confidence"),
            "red_flags": verdict_block.get("red_flags") or [],
            "decisions": verdict.get("decisions") or [],
            # Derived, not the reader's list: crossed-out and handwritten values
            "corrections": [
                f"{v['field']}: {v['raw']} ({'crossed out' if v['crossed_out'] else v['written']})"
                for v in all_values
                if v["crossed_out"] or v["written"] == "handwritten"
            ],
            "read_sha256": meta.get("sha256"),
            "current_sha256": current_sha.get(doc_path),
            "model": meta.get("model"),
        }
        reading = make_record(
            "reading",
            doc_path,
            source,
            attrs,
            doc_path=doc_path,
            po_numbers=keys["po_numbers"],
            delivery_note=keys.get("delivery_note"),
            reference=keys.get("reference"),
            batch=keys.get("batch"),
        )
        records.append(reading)
        for index, (line, values) in enumerate(zip(verdict.get("lines") or [], lines), start=1):
            records.append(
                make_record(
                    "doc_line",
                    f"{doc_path}#{index}",
                    source,
                    {
                        "item": line.get("item"),
                        "description": line.get("description"),
                        "supplier_part_no": clean(line.get("supplier_part_no")),
                        "material_raw": clean(line.get("material_id")),
                        "values": values,
                        "final": {f: v["number"] for f, v in final_values(values).items()},
                        "crossed": {v["field"]: v["number"] for v in values if v["crossed_out"]},
                    },
                    doc_path=doc_path,
                    po_numbers=keys["po_numbers"],
                    material_id=clean(line.get("material_id")),
                )
            )
        rows.append(
            {
                "path": source.path,
                "kind": "reading",
                "sha256": source.sha256,
                "adapter": True,
                "records": 1 + len(lines),
                "error": None,
            }
        )
    return records, rows


def map_supplier_part_numbers(records: list[dict], known_parts: set[str]) -> None:
    """
    Replace supplier part numbers on document lines with the buyer's part numbers, in place.

    The mapping is learned from the readings themselves: any line that names both a known part
    and a supplier part number (a contract annex, a packing list) teaches one pair. Nothing is
    typed in by hand.
    """
    lines = [r for r in records if r["kind"] == "doc_line"]
    mapping = {
        line["attrs"]["supplier_part_no"]: line["material_id"]
        for line in lines
        if line["material_id"] in known_parts and line["attrs"]["supplier_part_no"]
    }
    for line in lines:
        material = line["material_id"]
        if material and material not in known_parts and material in mapping:
            line["material_id"] = mapping[material]
            line["attrs"]["mapped_from"] = material
        elif not material and line["attrs"]["supplier_part_no"] in mapping:
            line["material_id"] = mapping[line["attrs"]["supplier_part_no"]]
            line["attrs"]["mapped_from"] = line["attrs"]["supplier_part_no"]

"""
uv run python -m verifier.impact          # parts, gaps and copies at risk
"""

import argparse
from pathlib import Path

from verifier.impact.shortfall import compute
from verifier.linker import build


def _n(value) -> str:
    return f"{value:,.0f}"


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="verifier.impact")
    parser.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=Path("data/portal"))
    parser.add_argument("--readings", type=Path, default=Path("data/store/image_recognizer"))
    args = parser.parse_args()

    graph = build(args.root, args.readings)
    result = compute(graph.records, graph.issues)

    print("Editions")
    for e in result.editions:
        at_risk, part = result.at_risk(e.product)
        risk = f"  at risk {_n(at_risk)} (binding part {part})" if at_risk else ""
        print(f"  {e.product:<12} day one {_n(e.day_one):>8}  packed {_n(e.packed):>8}  "
              f"remaining {_n(e.remaining):>7}{risk}")
    print("\nParts (system view → evidence view)")
    for p in result.parts:
        flag = "SHORT" if p.gap else "ok"
        print(f"  {p.part:<12} need {_n(p.needed):>7}  book {_n(p.book_stock):>8}  usable {_n(p.usable):>8}"
              f"  gap {_n(p.gap):>7}  {flag:<5}  plan said: {p.plan_status or '-'}  [{', '.join(p.editions)}]")
        for d in p.deductions:
            print(f"      - {_n(d.units)} {d.reason} ({d.issue})")
        for s in p.supply:
            print(f"      + option: {s['kind']} {_n(s['quantity'] or 0)} {s.get('reference') or s.get('document', '')}")
    for x in result.excluded:
        print(f"\n  not counted: {x['part']} for {x['edition']}: fitted inside {x['inside']} ({x['evidence']})")
    if result.shared_gaps:
        print("\nShared parts short (who gets them is a decision):")
        for p in result.shared_gaps:
            print(f"  {p.part}: {_n(p.gap)} short across {', '.join(p.editions)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
Act: one decision card per cause of copies at risk.

A card says what is at risk, why (system vs paper), what could close the gap, and who has to do
something, with the message ready to send. Who to ask follows the routing table in
verifier/README.md: what arrived → Hamburg receiving; what shipped → the supplier; what is
allowed → an approver (PP-07; a vacant role escalates to the Head of Procurement).

Nothing is sent automatically: a person reads the card and clicks send.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import pandas as pd

from verifier.impact.shortfall import PartNeed, Shortfall

HAMBURG = "DC Hamburg (receiving and logistics)"
APPROVER = "Head of Procurement (Category Lead is vacant, PP-07 §6)"


@dataclass
class Message:
    to_role: str
    to_email: str | None
    subject: str
    body: str


@dataclass
class Card:
    id: str
    title: str
    edition: str
    at_risk: float  # copies of `edition` this card can save
    part: str
    system_says: str
    paper_says: str
    evidence: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    options: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    decision: str | None = None  # what a person has to decide, if anything
    messages: list[Message] = field(default_factory=list)


def _n(value) -> str:
    return f"{value:,.0f}"


class _Directory:
    """Supplier contacts and documents, from the linked records."""

    def __init__(self, records: pd.DataFrame):
        rows = records.to_dict("records")
        self.suppliers = {}
        for r in rows:  # the newest version of a supplier wins for contact details
            if r["kind"] == "supplier":
                current = self.suppliers.get(r["supplier_id"])
                if current is None or (r["as_of"] or "") > (current["as_of"] or ""):
                    self.suppliers[r["supplier_id"]] = r
        self.parts = {r["material_id"]: r["attrs"].get("description") for r in rows if r["kind"] == "part"}
        self.primary = {}
        self.prices = {}
        for r in rows:
            if r["kind"] == "supplier_part":
                self.prices[(r["supplier_id"], r["material_id"])] = r["attrs"]
                if r["attrs"].get("primary") == "Y":
                    self.primary.setdefault(r["material_id"], r["supplier_id"])

    def contact(self, supplier_id: str | None) -> tuple[str, str | None, str | None]:
        s = self.suppliers.get(supplier_id) or {"attrs": {}}
        a = s["attrs"]
        return a.get("name") or supplier_id or "supplier", a.get("contact_email"), a.get("contact_name")

    def supplier_of_path(self, doc_path: str) -> str | None:
        return next((sid for sid in self.suppliers if sid and f"/{sid}_" in f"/{doc_path}"), None)


def _signature() -> str:
    return "\n\nBest regards,\nSoony Procurement"


def _edition_of(need: PartNeed, result: Shortfall) -> str:
    return need.editions[0] if len(need.editions) == 1 else " + ".join(need.editions)


def build_cards(result: Shortfall, issues: pd.DataFrame, records: pd.DataFrame) -> list[Card]:
    directory = _Directory(records)
    launch = min((e.launch_date for e in result.editions if e.launch_date), default="launch")
    cards: list[Card] = []
    for need in result.parts:
        part, desc = need.part, need.description or need.part
        edition = _edition_of(need, result)
        reasons = {d.reason: d for d in need.deductions}

        # 1. Gap that stock waiting at the port could close
        at_port = [s for s in need.supply if s["kind"] == "at_port"]
        if need.gap and at_port:
            s = at_port[0]
            cards.append(Card(
                id=f"collect-{part}",
                title=f"Collect {desc} from the port",
                edition=edition, at_risk=need.gap, part=part,
                system_says=f"Launch plan: {need.plan_status or 'ok'}, {_n(s['quantity'])} counted as due",
                paper_says=f"Only {_n(need.usable)} in stock for {_n(need.needed)} still to pack; "
                           f"{_n(s['quantity'])} are at the port ({s.get('note') or 'not collected'})",
                evidence=[f"Shipment {s['reference']}: {s.get('note') or ''}",
                          f"Book stock {_n(need.book_stock)} (as of {need.book_as_of})"],
                options=[f"Collect {_n(s['quantity'])} ({s['reference']}) and book a dock slot today"],
                messages=[Message(
                    HAMBURG, None,
                    f"Urgent: collect {s['reference']} ({desc}) for the {launch} pack-out",
                    f"Hello,\n\nshipment {s['reference']} with {_n(s['quantity'])} {desc} ({part}) "
                    f"is at the port and available for pick-up. DC stock is {_n(need.usable)}, and "
                    f"{_n(need.needed)} are still needed for the launch pack-out, so the line stops "
                    f"after about {_n(need.usable)} copies.\n\nPlease arrange pick-up and a dock slot "
                    f"for today and confirm the arrival time." + _signature(),
                )],
            ))

        # 2. Booked but never delivered: count it, and buy what is offered
        phantom = reasons.get("booked but not delivered")
        if phantom:
            offers = [s for s in need.supply if s["kind"] == "offer"]
            card = Card(
                id=f"phantom-{part}",
                title=f"{desc}: {_n(phantom.units)} booked that never arrived",
                edition=edition, at_risk=need.gap, part=part,
                system_says=f"Book stock {_n(need.book_stock)}; plan says {need.plan_status or 'ok'}",
                paper_says=phantom.context,
                evidence=[phantom.context, f"Receipt record {phantom.issue}"],
            )
            card.messages.append(Message(
                HAMBURG, None, f"Please count {desc} ({part}) and correct receipt {phantom.issue.split(':')[-1]}",
                f"Hello,\n\nreceipt {phantom.issue.split(':')[-1]} books more {desc} than the "
                f"delivery note shows ({phantom.context}).\n\nPlease count {part} physically and "
                f"correct the receipt. Our evidence says about {_n(need.usable)} are really in stock."
                + _signature(),
            ))
            for offer in offers:
                supplier = directory.supplier_of_path(offer["document"])
                name, email, person = directory.contact(supplier)
                price = directory.prices.get((supplier, part), {})
                value = (price.get("unit_price") or 0) * offer["quantity"]
                worth = f" (about {value:,.0f} {price.get('currency') or ''} at list price)" if value else ""
                card.options.append(f"Accept {name}'s offer: {_n(offer['quantity'])} from stock{worth}")
                card.messages.append(Message(
                    f"{name} ({person or 'sales'})", email,
                    f"Order: {_n(offer['quantity'])} {desc} from stock, per your offer",
                    f"Dear {person or 'Sir or Madam'},\n\nthank you for your offer. We would like to "
                    f"order the {_n(offer['quantity'])} {desc} ({part}) you have in stock, at the "
                    f"normal price, for delivery to DC Hamburg as soon as possible.\n\nPlease confirm "
                    f"the loading time and the truck's arrival time. A PO follows." + _signature(),
                ))
            cards.append(card)

        # 3. A failed lot: someone has to decide on a concession
        failed = reasons.get("failed inspection")
        if failed:
            cards.append(Card(
                id=f"concession-{part}",
                title=f"{desc}: decide on the failed lot",
                edition=edition, at_risk=need.gap, part=part,
                system_says=f"{_n(failed.units)} counted as usable stock",
                paper_says=f"Inspection failed: {failed.context}",
                evidence=[failed.context],
                options=[f"Concession: use the {_n(failed.units)} after sorting out defects",
                         f"No concession: {_n(need.gap)} copies short"],
                decision=f"Use the failed lot under a concession, or accept {_n(need.gap)} fewer copies?",
                messages=[Message(
                    APPROVER, None, f"Decision needed today: failed lot of {desc} ({part})",
                    f"Hello,\n\nthe lot ({failed.issue.split(':')[-1]}) failed incoming inspection: "
                    f"{failed.context}.\n\nWithout it we are {_n(need.gap)} {desc} short for the "
                    f"launch pack-out. The Category Lead role is vacant, so per PP-07 the decision on a "
                    f"concession sits with you.\n\nPlease decide: concession (sort and use) or no "
                    f"concession." + _signature(),
                )],
            ))

        # 4. Wrong part or old revision booked: correct the booking (no copies at risk if covered)
        for reason in ("wrong part booked", "old revision, must not be packed"):
            d = reasons.get(reason)
            if d:
                cards.append(Card(
                    id=f"{reason.split()[0]}-{part}",
                    title=f"{desc}: {_n(d.units)} {reason}",
                    edition=edition, at_risk=need.gap, part=part,
                    system_says=f"{_n(d.units)} counted as usable {part}",
                    paper_says=d.context,
                    evidence=[d.context],
                    options=["Block or rebook it so the line doesn't pack it"],
                    messages=[Message(
                        HAMBURG, None, f"Please block/rebook: {_n(d.units)} {desc} ({reason})",
                        f"Hello,\n\n{d.context}.\n\nPlease block it for the GH6 pack-out and correct "
                        f"the booking. After this we still have {_n(need.usable)} usable for "
                        f"{_n(need.needed)} needed." + _signature(),
                    )],
                ))

    # 5. A shared part is short: decide who gets it, and ask the supplier for more
    for need in result.shared_gaps:
        desc = need.description or need.part
        short = [i for i in issues.to_dict("records")
                 if i["rule"] == "plan_vs_paper" and i["material_id"] == need.part]
        supplier = None
        if short:
            reading = records[records.record_id == short[0]["related"]]
            supplier = directory.supplier_of_path(reading.doc_path.iloc[0]) if len(reading) else None
        supplier = supplier or directory.primary.get(need.part)
        name, email, person = directory.contact(supplier)
        later = [s for s in need.supply if s["kind"] == "after_launch"]
        card = Card(
            id=f"allocate-{need.part}",
            title=f"{desc}: {_n(need.gap)} short across {len(need.editions)} editions",
            edition=" + ".join(need.editions), at_risk=need.gap, part=need.part,
            system_says=short[0]["context"] if short else f"Plan says {need.plan_status or 'ok'}",
            paper_says=f"{_n(need.usable)} in stock for {_n(need.needed)} still to pack",
            evidence=[i["context"] for i in short] + [f"Book stock {_n(need.book_stock)}"],
            options=[f"{s['reference']}: {_n(s['quantity'])} arriving {s['eta']} (after launch)" for s in later],
            decision=f"Which edition gets the {_n(need.usable)} {desc}?",
        )
        card.messages.append(Message(
            APPROVER, None, f"Decision needed: allocate {desc} between editions",
            f"Hello,\n\nwe have {_n(need.usable)} {desc} for {_n(need.needed)} still to pack "
            f"({', '.join(need.editions)}): {_n(need.gap)} short. Please decide which edition gets "
            f"them first." + _signature(),
        ))
        if email:
            card.messages.append(Message(
                f"{name} ({person or 'sales'})", email,
                f"{desc} ({need.part}): any quantity earlier than planned?",
                f"Dear {person or 'Sir or Madam'},\n\nwe are {_n(need.gap)} {desc} short for our launch "
                f"pack-out, which ends on {launch}. Can any part of the open balance reach DC Hamburg "
                f"earlier, for example on an earlier flight? Please reply with quantity and arrival "
                f"time." + _signature(),
            ))
        cards.append(card)

    return sorted(cards, key=lambda c: -c.at_risk)

"""
uv run python -m verifier.act        # build decision cards → data/store/decision_cards.html (+ .json)
"""

import argparse
from pathlib import Path

from verifier.act.cards import build_cards
from verifier.act.render import render, to_json
from verifier.impact.shortfall import compute
from verifier.linker import build


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="verifier.act")
    parser.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=Path("data/portal"))
    parser.add_argument("--readings", type=Path, default=Path("data/store/image_recognizer"))
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=Path("data/store/decision_cards.html"))
    args = parser.parse_args()

    graph = build(args.root, args.readings)
    result = compute(graph.records, graph.issues)
    cards = build_cards(result, graph.issues, graph.records)
    args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.out.write_text(render(result, cards, graph.built_at))
    args.out.with_suffix(".json").write_text(to_json(result, cards))
    for card in cards:
        print(f"{card.at_risk:>8,.0f}  {card.title}  →  {', '.join(m.to_role for m in card.messages)}")
    print(f"\n{len(cards)} cards → {args.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

        "corrections": [], "decisions": [{"subject": "lot", "outcome": "fail", "decided_by": None,

    assert "CMP-MAG" not in needs  # fitted inside CMP-B by the supplier, never stocked

def test_failed_lot_is_not_usable_and_puts_copies_at_risk(tmp_path):

    assert [d.reason for d in part_a.deductions] == ["failed inspection"]
    assert part_a.usable == 1050 - 500  # batch 7000000001 holds 500
    assert part_a.gap == 50
    assert result.shared_gaps == [part_a]  # CMP-A is used by both editions


def test_cards_route_and_render(tmp_path):
    root = portal_with_plan(tmp_path)

## Review: step 2, `impact/` and `act/`

**Verdict:** This is the strongest piece so far, and it should be the core of the pitch. I found one presentation problem and one missed opportunity that could matter more than anything else on Sunday. I made no changes.

- **Checks:** 107 tests pass and ruff is clean. I count 107, not the 110 you reported, and I haven't traced the difference.

### What's right

- **The numbers hold.** `verifier.impact` reproduces my rough arithmetic, now from the BOM and the data.
  - Art books: gap 5,900 (book 77,800, minus 72,000 phantom).
  - Statues: gap 3,400 (book 13,900, minus the 5,600 failed lot).
  - Game cards: gap 6,800 (42,900 against 49,700).
  - The magnets are correctly left out, because `CMP-MAG-005` is fitted inside `CMP-GAM-007`.
- **New finding.** 64,000 sleeves in stock are revision B, but ECN-2026-118 says revision B must not be packed (`old_revision_in_stock`). It is derived from a change notice plus a supplier confirmation, with nothing hardcoded.
- **Per-cause cards:** Each card shows system says vs paper says, options and a routed message. The routing follows your own table:
  - Hamburg for counts.
  - The supplier for what shipped.
  - The Head of Procurement for the statue concession, with the vacant Category Lead rule from PP-07 applied.
- **The Karton offer card is correct.** I first suspected the email's "at the normal price" contradicted a 35% surcharge. It doesn't: the surcharge is on item 1 (rush printing), and the art books (item 2) are at the Annex A price. So 8,000 × 2.10 = 16,800 EUR is right.

### Needs fixing

1. **The "at risk" headline double-counts closable gaps.**
   - **Problem:** STD shows `at risk 32,000` (clear cases, `CMP-GAM-003`), yet 350,000 are at the Hamburg terminal waiting for pickup. `at_risk()` ignores supply options entirely.
   - **Why it matters:** The card is titled correctly, but a headline total would overstate the risk by 32,000, and a jury member will notice.
   - **Fix:** Show the gap before and after the options that can arrive before launch.
     - Art books: closed by Karton's 8,000.
     - Cases: closed by collecting the container.
     - Statues: only via a concession (the other 10,000 arrive 27 Nov).
     - Game cards: nothing arrives in time (36,000 on 23 Nov), so about **6,800 STD copies are really at risk**.

2. **No deadline on the cards.** The Karton offer is valid 24 hours from 21 Nov, loads within 4 hours of ordering, and the truck drives about 9 hours.
   - **Arithmetic (mine, so treat as approximate):** Real art-book stock of 5,800 covers about 6.4 hours of the CE cell at 900 per hour. If Sunday packing starts at 06:00, the next 8,000 must be at the dock by about 12:30. Subtracting 13 hours (4 loading plus 9 driving) gives an **order deadline around Saturday 23:30**.
   - **Why it matters:** A "latest order time" on each card (needed-by minus lead time) turns a list of issues into "do this in the next hour". It is the best demo moment available, and the data already contains every input.

3. **Cards that say "block it" don't ask whether it's already packed.** The stock update shows 90,000 sleeves used today while 64,000 revision-B sleeves sit in stock. The cards should ask Hamburg which sleeve batch the lines have been pulling, and whether any packed copies carry the old mark.

### Smaller points

- **Sending:** "Nothing is sent automatically" (mailto and copy text) is safe, but the challenge's one rule is "agents write, escalate, act". Jonas owns supplier email and calls (see `PROGRESS.md`). Hand him `data/store/decision_cards.json` as his input, since `messages` already has `to_email`, subject and body. Sender addresses must be registered in the portal first.
- **Tests:**
  - `act/` has none.
  - The new linker rules `old_revision_in_stock` and `plan_vs_paper` have no direct tests.
  - The planning adapters and `parse_count` aren't tested directly.
  - The three impact tests cover the flow, not those pieces.
- **Cards with no gap.** The two sleeve cards show `at_risk: 0` (usable 48,000 against 38,000 needed). That is correct, but label them "stock blocked, no gap" so they don't read as noise.
- **Uncommitted.** Everything under `act/`, `impact/` and `planning.py` is not committed.

Caveman was read.

Think of the whole verifier as three questions:
1. **Linker + reader: "What's true?"** They compare SAP with the paper and list the contradictions.
2. **Impact: "How bad is it?"** It turns those contradictions into missing copies and a run-out time.
3. **Act: "What do we do, by when, and who does it?"** It turns that into decision cards with ready messages.

---

## Impact (`verifier/impact/`): how bad is it?

It answers the brief's line *"the system says we're fine, my gut says we're not"* with numbers.

### Step 1: How many copies are still to pack?
- **Day-one demand** comes from `products.csv`: Standard 640,000, Collector's 72,000.
- **Already packed** comes from the newest stock update (Sat 20:50): 602,000 and 60,300.
- **Still to pack:** 38,000 Standard and 11,700 Collector's.

### Step 2: How many parts does that need?
- The **BOM** (`bom.csv`) says what goes into one copy. For example, one Collector's has 1 card, 1 art book, 1 statue, 1 box and so on.
- So each part's need is copies still to pack × parts per copy. Art books: 11,700. Game cards: 38,000 + 11,700 = 49,700, because both editions use them.
- **Magnets are skipped.** The BOM lists 4 per Collector's, but PackRight's own part list says *"fitted by supplier into the box, not stocked separately"*. So they aren't missing; they come inside the box. That clears the plan's old "−100,800 CHECK" alarm.

### Step 3: How many are really there?
- **Book stock** is what SAP believes. Art books: 77,800.
- Then it **subtracts what the evidence says isn't really usable**, taken from the linker's issues:

| Reason | Example | Subtracted |
|---|---|---|
| Booked but never delivered | Art books: paper 8,000, SAP 80,000 | 72,000 |
| Failed inspection | Statue lot 5000413063 | 5,600 |
| Wrong part booked | GH5 pallet booked as GH6 sleeves | 4,000 |
| Old revision, must not be packed | Rev. B sleeves | 64,000 |

- **Usable** = book stock minus those. Art books: 77,800 − 72,000 = **5,800**.

### Step 4: The gap
**Gap** = needed − usable. Art books: 11,700 − 5,800 = **5,900 short**.

The part with the biggest gap in an edition decides how many copies are at risk, because a Collector's copy needs *all* its parts.

**Result:**

| Part | Needed | Plan said | Usable | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Clear case | 38,000 | ok | 6,000 | **32,000** |
| Game card | 49,700 | ok | 42,900 | **6,800** |
| Art book | 11,700 | ok | 5,800 | **5,900** |
| Statue | 11,700 | ok | 8,300 | **3,400** |
| Sleeve | 38,000 | ok | 48,000 | none (even after blocking 68,000) |

### Step 5: When does it run out? (`timing.py`)
- **Packing hours** come from the launch plan's shift sheet: Sat 06–22, Sun 06–20.
- **Speed** comes from the plan: Standard 6,000 per hour, Collector's 900 per hour.
- **"Now"** is the stock update's time (Sat 20:50), not the computer clock. The same data always gives the same answer.
- Run-out = usable ÷ speed, counted through the shifts and skipping the night.
  - Art books: 5,800 ÷ 900 = 6.4 hours of packing. That's 1h10 left on Saturday plus 5h16 on Sunday, so **they run out Sun 11:16**.
  - Clear cases: 6,000 ÷ 6,000 = 1 hour, so **they run out Sat 21:50**, tonight.

### Step 6: What could still fix it in time?
It looks for supply in the data:
- **At the port:** 350,000 clear cases at the Hamburg terminal (launch plan Inbound sheet) → "collect".
- **An offer:** Karton's 8,000 art books from stock (read from their Polish offer). The lead time is also read from the paper: *"loaded within 4 h"* + *"about 9 hours driving"* = 13 h.
- **A decision:** the failed statue lot can be used under a concession.
- **Too late:** 36,000 Boise cards on 23 Nov, the 20,000 Hwaseong balance on 24 Nov. These are shown but don't count.

**Act-by** = run-out time − lead time. Art books: Sun 11:16 − 13 h = **order by Sat 22:16**.

So every edition gets two numbers:

| | At risk now | If you act in time |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | 32,000 | 0 |
| Collector's | 5,900 | 0 |
| Game cards (shared) | 6,800 | **6,800**, because nothing arrives in time |

---

## Act (`verifier/act/`): what to do, by when, who

It turns each cause into **one decision card**. Each card has:

| Part of the card | Art book example |
|---|---|
| Copies at risk, now → if you act | 5,900 → 0 |
| **Act by** | Sat 21 Nov 22:16 |
| Line runs out | Sun 22 Nov 11:16 |
| **System says** | Book stock 77,800, plan says ok |
| **Paper says** | Paper 8,000 (handwritten; printed 80,000 crossed out), SAP 80,000, ordered 8,000 |
| Options | Accept Karton's 8,000 from stock (≈16,800 EUR at list price). Ordered now, they arrive Sun 09:50 |
| Messages | 1. Hamburg: count the art books and correct the receipt. 2. Karton: "we'd like to order your 8,000 from stock, please confirm loading and arrival" |

**Who gets asked** follows our routing table from the verifier README:
- **What arrived → Hamburg** (count, block, collect)
- **What shipped → the supplier** (email from their profile, e.g. Karton's contact)
- **What's allowed → the approver.** The Category Lead role is vacant, so PP-07 sends it to the Head of Procurement (the statue concession, the game card allocation)

**The 6 cards today:**
1. Collect the clear cases from the port → Hamburg (act by Sat 21:50)
2. Game cards short across editions → Maren decides who gets them, and Hwaseong is asked for an earlier flight
3. Art books never delivered → Hamburg counts, Karton gets the order (act by Sat 22:16)
4. Failed statue lot → Maren: concession or not
5. and 6. Sleeves: GH5 pallet and rev. B batch → Hamburg blocks them and checks whether any were already packed ("no gap, stock blocked")

**Safety:** nothing is sent on its own. A person reads the card and clicks *Email* (it opens a ready email) or *Copy text*. The same cards also go to `decision_cards.json`, so an email agent (Jonas's) can send them.

**The page** (`decision_cards.html`):
- **Top:** "Will we make the launch?", with now vs if-you-act per edition.
- **Below:** the cards, most copies at risk first, each with its red "Act by" badge.

---

**Why it matters for the pitch:** it goes from *"we found contradictions"* to *"32,000 copies are at risk, you have until 21:50 to send a truck, here's the email."* That's the "agents act" rule, plus a number the customer cares about.

Caveman was read.

**Short answer: act is rules, not AI.** I wrote the rules from the reasoning we did earlier. Here's how each part came about, and where it's weaker than it looks.

## 1. One card per *cause*, not per number

**Reasoning:** a shortage alone says nothing about what to do. "Art books 5,900 short" could mean order more, recount, or move stock. What decides the action is **why** it's short. So the card type comes from the cause impact already found:

| Cause (from the evidence) | What that implies | Card |
|---|---|---|
| Stock is waiting at the port | It exists, it's just not here | **Collect** |
| Booked but never delivered | SAP is wrong, so count it. A supplier offers stock, so buy it | **Count + order** |
| Failed inspection | It's physically here but not allowed | **Decide: concession?** |
| A part shared by two editions is short | Not enough for both, and nothing arrives in time | **Decide: who gets it** + ask the supplier for earlier delivery |
| Wrong part or old revision | No gap, but it must not be packed | **Block + "was it already packed?"** |

## 2. Who to ask: the routing table

This is the "who would know / who may decide" principle from the verifier README, which we wrote together:
- **What physically arrived → Hamburg.** Only they can count a pallet or see the port container.
- **What was shipped or offered → the supplier.** They know their own stock and flights. The email address comes from **their profile in the data**.
- **What's allowed → an approver.** That came from our earlier reading of policy **PP-07** and the org chart: concessions need the Category Lead, the role is vacant, and §6 says to escalate to the Head of Procurement.

## 3. What decision to take: it doesn't take one

**It never decides.** It lays out the options with their consequences, and a person decides:
- **Statue:** concession (use 5,600 after sorting) vs. no concession (3,400 copies short)
- **Game cards:** which edition gets the 42,900
- **Art books:** the offer is a *proposal*. The email is ready, but a buyer clicks send.

Two reasons: these decisions cost money or quality and belong to a named role, and the jury explicitly asks about "the moment a human has to decide".

## Honest weak spots

| What | The problem |
|---|---|
| **"Head of Procurement" and "DC Hamburg" are typed into the code** | They come from our analysis, not from the data at runtime. That breaks our own "nothing hardcoded" rule. **Fix:** read the approver from the PP-07 and org chart readings (both already read), with their approval limits. |
| Internal email addresses are empty | The data has no addresses for Hamburg or Maren |
| Email texts are fixed templates, in English only | Karton writes Polish, Hwaseong Korean. An AI could draft each message in the supplier's language |
| "Collect" assumes pickup is possible today | Nobody has checked with the terminal yet. The card says so as an assumption |
| Card types are a fixed list | A new kind of cause needs a new rule |

**The most important fix before the demo is #1**, because the jury checks for hardcoding. Shall I do it?

# ask-soony: the system says fine, the paper says otherwise

Our entry for the **Lio challenge "Keep the Line Running"** (START Hack Munich 2026).

Soony launches Grand Heist 6 on **Sunday 20:00**. Its launch plan says every part is **ok**. We read every delivery note, confirmation, inspection report and contract, scans and four languages included, and checked the system against the paper. On the same data:

| | Launch plan | Paper trail |
|---|---|---|
| Standard Edition | ok | **32,000 copies at risk**: only 6,000 clear cases in stock, while 350,000 sit uncollected at the Hamburg port |
| Collector's Edition | ok | **5,900 at risk**: SAP booked 80,000 art books, and the delivery note says 8,000 (handwritten correction) |
| Game cards | ok | **6,800 short**: only 28,000 of 48,000 flew |
| If everyone acts in time | | **only the 6,800 game cards remain at risk** |

Every number comes with its evidence, a deadline ("order by Sat 22:16") and who has to act.

## How it works

```
portal data ──► linker ──► image recognizer ──► impact ──► act
(SAP, Excel,    connect     read every scan     what's      decision cards:
 PDFs, scans)   the records and PDF with Claude really      who, what, by when
                and find    (claims + verdict)  missing,
                the gaps                        by when
```

1. **Linker** (`verifier/linker/`): connects every record about the same order, delivery or lot (PO → confirmation → shipment → delivery note → receipt → stock → inspection), and lists what doesn't fit.
2. **Image recognizer** (`verifier/image_recognizer/`): Claude reads each document once and records what's on the paper, including handwriting, crossed-out values and stamps.
3. **Impact** (`verifier/impact/`):
   - **Usable stock:** book stock minus everything the evidence says isn't real or usable.
   - **Gap:** usable stock against what's still to pack, from the BOM.
   - **Run-out time:** when each part runs out at the packing rate.
4. **Act** (`verifier/act/`): one decision card per cause, with *system says* vs *paper says*, the options, the decision needed, and a ready message to the right person. People and roles are read from the org chart and the approval policy. A person decides; nothing is sent on its own.

## Run it

```bash
uv sync --group dev
cp .env.example .env                    # put SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN in it (portal → Settings)
uv run ask-soony download               # fetch the portal data into data/portal/
```

| Step | Command | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Read the documents (Claude, via the Agent SDK) | `uv run python -m verifier.image_recognizer` | `data/store/image_recognizer/` (resumable, one read per file version) |
| Link and check | `uv run python -m verifier.linker build` | Issues, live ones first, soonest first |
| Follow one order | `uv run python -m verifier.linker trace 4500318768` | The whole chain of that PO, with its issues |
| What's really missing | `uv run python -m verifier.impact` | Need, book stock, usable, gap per part |
| Decision cards | `uv run python -m verifier.act && open data/store/decision_cards.html` | The page, plus `decision_cards.json` for other agents |
| Tests | `uv run pytest` | 127 tests on made-up data |

**The image recognizer uses your Claude Code login.** No API key is needed. Its results are cached by checksum, so the other steps run without any model calls.

## What makes it hold up

- **Nothing hardcoded:**
  - Files are recognised by their columns or tables, so a new drop needs no code change.
  - Supplier names, part mappings, role holders and lead times are all read from the data.
- **Contradictions are shown, not resolved silently:**
  - When two sources disagree, both versions are kept and the difference is named.
  - Link certainty is labelled: `exact` vs `po_level`.
- **Reader mistakes are fixed in code:** for example "19.000" is 19,000, and signatures aren't treated as corrections. The raw text is always kept as evidence.
- **Deterministic:** "now" is the time of the newest stock figures, so the same data always gives the same answer.
- **A human decides:** the system recommends and drafts; concessions and allocations go to the role the policy names.

## More

| Topic | Where |
|---|---|
| Verifier design: evidence rules, routing, linking keys | [verifier/README.md](verifier/README.md) |
| Linker build order and principles | [verifier/linker/linker_strategy.md](verifier/linker/linker_strategy.md) |
| What the document reading found | [verifier/image_recognizer/findings.md](verifier/image_recognizer/findings.md) |
| Hand-off for sending messages | [verifier/act/HANDOFF.md](verifier/act/HANDOFF.md) |
| Product strategy | [strategy.md](strategy.md) |
| Data watcher (polls the portal, keeps every version) | [docs/INSTRUCTIONS.md](docs/INSTRUCTIONS.md#data-watcher-src_ask_soony) |
| Team setup and conventions | [docs/INSTRUCTIONS.md](docs/INSTRUCTIONS.md), [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) |

Soony and all its data are fictional, from the challenge. The data is used only for this hackathon.

# ask-soony

Our entry for the **Lio challenge "Keep the Line Running"** at START Hack Munich 2026.

Soony, a (fictional) games publisher, launches Grand Heist 6 on **Sunday 22 Nov, 20:00**. Every copy is packed in one distribution center in Hamburg, six suppliers deliver the parts, and the last 20% is not packed yet. Soony's data lives in SAP, spreadsheets, PDFs and scans, in four languages. Soony's head of procurement: "We find out at the dock."

We build agents that read that data, decide what is at risk and act on it before it is too late.

## What it is

**Ask Soony is an AI procurement team for the last mile of a launch.** Agents read everything the customer has (SAP exports, spreadsheets, supplier PDFs and scans in four languages, emails, news), find where the paperwork and the plan disagree, work out what that costs in copies and hours, and act: they write to suppliers, ask the warehouse, chase, and pass decisions to the person who signs. A human decides anything that costs money or changes the plan, with one tap.

Live: `https://ask-soony.stenglein.dev` (password protected; ask the team).

### Who uses it

| | Today | Launch | Sign-off page (phone) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **For** | The senior buyer, all day | The head of procurement, a few times a day | Whoever signs, when their phone buzzes |
| **Question** | What do I do now? | Will we make the deadline, what breaks first, who must decide? | Do I approve this? |

### The loop: notice → show → act → learn

1. **Notice.** Every portal change runs all checks within minutes. Documents are held against SAP (late or short, old revision, failed lot, goods receipt vs. delivery note), shipments are reconciled from every source (goods receipts, warehouse answers, supplier documents and replies, the hand-kept tracker, the system export), and silence is measured against the clock. Numbers that are only projections (a pack-out log hours old, book stock without a count) are called what they are.
2. **Show.** One calm decision at a time: the contradiction in one sentence, every number linked to the highlighted spot in its source document, what it means for the launch (when the packing line runs out of the part, how many copies that costs), and a recommendation with its price. Ranked by what the launch loses, not by which detector found it.
3. **Act.** Approve sends the email (reviewable: text, subject, recipient from known contacts only), asks the warehouse through a one-tap count page with photo OCR, or passes it on to the approver named in the approval policy, who answers on their phone. Supplier replies come back onto the case; confirmed orders become inbound with an estimated arrival; if it arrives too late to help, a follow-up decision appears. A voice assistant can talk a decision through and act only after a spoken yes.
4. **Learn.** After the second similar decision the system offers a routine. Routines start by asking (prepare, you send with one tap), then tell, then run quietly. Money and plan changes always come to a person.

### What makes it trustworthy

- **Nothing is hardcoded.** Products, parts, suppliers, sites, deadlines, shifts and policies are read from the data at runtime; files are recognised by their content, not their names.
- **Contradictions are shown, not resolved silently.** Every source keeps its age and its say.
- **The data can change shape.** A data check warns when a file can no longer be read, a column disappears, or a new kind of file arrives that nothing reads. Supplier master changes (status, contacts, bank details) become cases; a new address is never a send target without a human OK.
- **The mailbox is shared.** Emails sent by hand are read back from the Sent folder and tied to their case; sending the same thing twice needs a second click.

### Where it lives

| Area | Code |
|---|---|
| Server, state, ranking, sign-off routing | `src/ask_soony/api.py`, `signoff.py` |
| Document vs. ERP checks, grounding | `papercheck.py`, `anchors.py`, `verifier/` |
| Launch clock, editions, parts, inbound | `launch.py`, `launch_view.py`, `commitments.py`, `tracking.py` |
| Asking the warehouse (counts, arrivals) | `floor.py` |
| Supplier email, replies, shared mailbox | `cardtools.py`, `replies.py`, `outbox.py` |
| Routines (sandboxed, trust ladder) | `routines.py` |
| Data shape and master data checks | `datacheck.py`, `supplier_master.py`, `memo.py` |
| Voice, push, Teams, calls | `voice.py`, `push.py`, `teams.py`, `calls.py` |
| UI (React, Tailwind) | `web/src/components/` (`Today`, `Launch`, `Routines`, `SupplyMap`, `CountPage`, `OkPage`) |

Tests: `uv run pytest -q`. UI: `cd web && npm run build`.

**Demo instance** (`scripts/demo.sh reset`): a second server on `:8001` (`ask-soony-demo.stenglein.dev`) with every case open again and no real supplier email (`ASK_MAIL_DRY=on` records mails in `dry_outbox.json`). Push still reaches subscribed phones, so the count page and the sign-off page can be shown. Run `reset` between rehearsals; `snapshot` rebuilds it from the live state.

## Getting started

1. Clone the repo and install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), then `uv sync --group dev`
2. Create your `.env` from the template: `cp .env.example .env`. It is gitignored; never commit it or paste keys in chat.
3. Put the keys into `.env`:

   | Variable | Where to get it | Needed for |
   |---|---|---|
   | `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN` | Portal → Settings → API token | Everything (download, poll, watch) |
   | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | [Claude Console](https://console.anthropic.com/) → API keys | `analyze` and `watch` with the default Claude backend |
   | `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER` + `ASK_LLM_API_KEY` | OpenAI key, or empty for a local llama.cpp server | Only if you use another backend (see below) |

   `SOONY_PORTAL_URL` is already filled in by the template.
4. Set up Entire so your agent sessions are tracked: see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#entire-session-tracking)

### Download the portal data once

Needs only `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN`, no LLM key:

```bash
uv run ask-soony download              # all current files into data/portal/, under their portal paths
uv run ask-soony download some/folder  # or into another folder
```

Run it again any time to bring the folder up to date: only new or changed files are fetched (the first run uses `archive.zip`). Files removed from the portal stay in the folder. Every version also lands in the version store (`data/store/`, see below). All of `data/` is gitignored: the data is confidential.

## Platform: decision inbox (`ask-soony run`)

Note for Farhan: change to the shortfall calculation (Sun 22 Nov, early morning)

Hi Farhan, while you were asleep we changed one calculation in impact/shortfall.py. Nothing is
committed or pushed; it is all in the working tree for you to review.

What was wrong
- PartNeed.gap was needed - usable stock. It ignored supply that is already on its way and
  lands in Hamburg before packing ends (Sun 20:00).
- Example: the game card card said 34,800 short (153,200 needed - 118,400 book stock as of
  20 Nov). Hwaseong's air freight 020-48113256 (PO 4500318735) lands on 21 Nov; its shipping
  advice says 28,000 of 48,000 were flown, the 20,000 balance lands Tue 24 Nov (after launch).
  The real gap is 6,800, which is also what papercheck.py rule a computes.

What changed
- shortfall.py: new PartNeed.arriving and PartNeed.not_counted lists, new property
  arriving_in_time, and gap = needed - usable - arriving_in_time. gap_if_acted, at_risk and
  the cards follow automatically.
- New function _arriving() fills both lists. Sources: plan_inbound rows, plus ERP shipment rows
  (newest per reference; quantity from their open PO lines when the plan has no row). It counts
  an inbound only if:
  - ETA is on or before launch day (same cut-off as the existing after_launch rule)
  - not cancelled and not "arrived" at the port (that stays a collect fix, not available stock)
  - no goods receipt for its PO and part between its ETD and the stock date (that would already
    be in the book stock); a receipt after the stock date counts with the received quantity
  - not overdue (ETA before the stock date and no receipt: treated as lost, not as supply)
  - the supplier's shipping document for the same reference does not say less; if it does,
    only the shipped quantity counts and the balance goes to not_counted with its expected date
  - if such a shipping document exists but has no reading yet, it is NOT counted (reason
    "not read yet"), because the paper may be a short-shipment advice like this one
- cards.py (allocate card only): paper_says, the decision question and the approver message use
  stock + arriving; evidence lists what was counted as arriving and what was not, and why.
- Tests: 5 new tests in impact/tests/test_shortfall.py (in-time vs after-launch vs cancelled vs
  unread advice; shipped short with balance, card disappears when the gap closes; receipt before
  and after the stock date; overdue shipment). Full suite: 219 passed, ruff clean.

Important: readings
- There is no data/store/image_recognizer on Jonas's Mac, so the shipping advice has no reading
  there. With the rule above the dispatch run there still says 34,800 short, and now names the

# Image recognizer (discovery run)

Reads every document (scans, photos, PDFs) with one OpenAI vision call each (`OPENAI_API_KEY` from `.env`). Images are resized and PDF pages without a text layer are rendered to images by the shared `ask_soony.extract`; the answer is forced into the JSON schema in `schema.py`. The goal is to see what the documents say and what kinds of errors keep coming up.

```bash
uv run python -m ask_soony.verifier.image_recognizer                       # all ~277 documents, resumable
uv run python -m ask_soony.verifier.image_recognizer --only WZ-261116-473   # one document
uv run python -m ask_soony.verifier.image_recognizer --images-only --limit 5
```

Options: `--model` (default `gpt-5.4-mini`), `--effort` (default `medium`), `--concurrency` (default 4), `--force` (read again).

## Output: `data/store/image_recognizer/` (gitignored, confidential)

One folder per document, `<path>__<sha12>/`:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `verdict.json` | Everything on the paper as values: raw text **and** a plain `number` (`80.000` → 80000), printed/handwritten/stamped, crossed out, legible. Plus references, statements, `decisions` (inspection pass/fail, approvals), corrections, and the verdict (status, red flags, observations) |
| `meta.json` | Checksum, model, time, token usage, status, error |

Plus `index.jsonl` (one line per document read) and `run_summary.json` (counts by type, verdict and status, plus errors).

"""
Paper check: read every supplier-side document in the portal and hold it against the ERP.

Suppliers and the DC write on paper (order confirmations, shipping advices, packing lists,
delivery notes, inspection reports, notices); SAP only knows what someone typed in. This agent
turns each document into claims, then runs small generic rules that look for a contradiction
between a claim and an ERP row. Every contradiction becomes an inbox card (findings.json,
decisions.json, impacts.json in the state folder) with both sides quoted, so nobody has to pick
one side silently.

1. Claims. Document text comes from the anchor index (PDF text layer, OCR for scans, table rows).
   Deterministic extraction first: references to known PO, goods receipt and delivery note
   numbers, table rows (item, part, description, quantity, price, currency, date), part lines
   with ordered / shipped / balance columns found by their header words, artwork revisions and
   status sentences (on hold, short shipment, lot does not meet AQL, ...). Then, when an OpenAI
   key is set, one LLM call per distinct free text (cached by content hash, so the same
   boilerplate on fifty confirmations costs one call) and one vision call per receiving scan whose
   goods receipt is still in stock (handwritten corrections). LLM statements are only kept when
   their quote is found in the document text.
2. Rules (see RULES): late or short delivery, old revision, receipt booked wrong, failed lot
   counted as stock, held at supplier.
3. Impact: remaining need per launch edition (day-one demand minus packed, times BOM usage)
   against stock plus open PO lines due before launch, with and without the contradicted
   quantity. A shortfall makes the card red; otherwise it is amber.

Nothing about Soony is written here: file names, columns, ids and values are discovered at run
time. `python -m ask_soony.papercheck` writes the cards; `run(write=False)` only returns them.
"""

"""
Readings (M3): what the image recognizer read from each document, as linker records.

One 'reading' record per document (keys from the references inside it) and one 'doc_line' record
per line on it (part and values). Fixes for known reader errors are applied here, on load:
- counts are re-parsed from the raw text ('19.000' is 19000, see normalize.count_number)
- corrections are derived from the values (crossed out or handwritten), not taken from the
  reader's own list, which mostly holds signatures and stamps
- supplier part numbers are mapped to the buyer's (map_supplier_part_numbers)

The raw text of every value is kept next to the number, so nothing the reader saw is lost.
"""

import hashlib
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from ask_soony.verifier.linker.normalize import clean, count_number
from ask_soony.verifier.linker.records import make_record

REFERENCE_KEYS = {
    "po_number": "po_numbers",
    "delivery_note": "delivery_note",
    "air_waybill": "reference",
    "container": "reference",
    "batch": "batch",
    "goods_receipt": "batch",  # a goods receipt number is the batch number
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReadingSource:
    """Where a reading came from, shaped like a discovered Source for make_record."""

    path: str
    sha256: str


def _references(verdict: dict) -> dict:
    keys: dict = {"po_numbers": []}
    for ref in verdict.get("references") or []:
        column = REFERENCE_KEYS.get(ref.get("type"))
        value = clean(ref.get("value"))
        if column is None or value is None:
            continue
        if column == "po_numbers":
            if value not in keys["po_numbers"]:
                keys["po_numbers"].append(value)
        else:
            keys.setdefault(column, value)
    return keys


def _value(raw: dict) -> dict:
    field = raw.get("field")
    return {
        "field": field if field != "other" else f"other:{raw.get('field_label') or '?'}",
        "raw": raw.get("value"),
        "number": count_number(field, raw.get("value"), raw.get("number")),
        "unit": raw.get("unit"),
        "written": raw.get("written"),
        "crossed_out": bool(raw.get("crossed_out")),
        "legible": raw.get("legible"),
    }


def final_values(values: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """Per field, the value that stands: not crossed out; handwritten beats printed."""
    standing: dict = {}
    for value in values:
        if value["crossed_out"]:
            continue
        current = standing.get(value["field"])
        if current is None or (
            value["written"] == "handwritten" and current["written"] != "handwritten"
        ):
            standing[value["field"]] = value
    return standing


def _current_readings(readings_dir: Path, current_sha: dict[str, str]) -> list[Path]:
    """
    One reading per document. A document read twice (its file changed in between) keeps only
    the reading of its current version; with no current reading, the old ones stay, marked stale.
    """
    by_doc: dict[str, list[tuple[Path, str | None]]] = {}
    for meta_path in sorted(readings_dir.glob("*/meta.json")):
        try:
            meta = json.loads(meta_path.read_text())
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if meta.get("status") == "ok" and meta.get("path"):
            by_doc.setdefault(meta["path"], []).append((meta_path, meta.get("sha256")))
    chosen = []
    for doc_path, readings in by_doc.items():
        current = [m for m, sha in readings if sha == current_sha.get(doc_path)]
        chosen += current or [m for m, _ in readings]
    return chosen


def load_readings(readings_dir: Path, current_sha: dict[str, str]) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict]]:
    """
    Records from every successful reading. Returns (records, source rows for the summary).

    current_sha maps each portal path to its current checksum, so a reading of an older version
    of a file is still loaded but marked (attrs.read_sha256 differs), never silently trusted.
    """
    records, rows = [], []
    for meta_path in _current_readings(readings_dir, current_sha):
        verdict_path = meta_path.parent / "verdict.json"
        try:
            meta = json.loads(meta_path.read_text())
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if meta.get("status") != "ok" or not verdict_path.exists():
            continue
        verdict = json.loads(verdict_path.read_text())
        doc_path = meta["path"]
        source = ReadingSource(
            f"{readings_dir.name}/{meta_path.parent.name}/verdict.json",
            hashlib.sha256(verdict_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        )
        keys = _references(verdict)
        lines = [
            [_value(v) for v in line.get("values") or []] for line in verdict.get("lines") or []
        ]
        all_values = [v for line in lines for v in line]
        received = next((v["raw"] for v in all_values if v["field"] == "date_received"), None)
        verdict_block = verdict.get("verdict") or {}
        attrs = {
            "doc_type": verdict.get("document_type"),
            "document_number": verdict.get("document_number"),
            "document_date": verdict.get("document_date"),
            "issuer": verdict.get("issuer"),
            "date_received": received,
            "status": verdict_block.get("status"),
            "confidence": verdict_block.get("confidence"),
            "red_flags": verdict_block.get("red_flags") or [],
            "decisions": verdict.get("decisions") or [],

def map_supplier_part_numbers(records: list[dict], known_parts: set[str]) -> None:
    """
    Replace supplier part numbers on document lines with the buyer's part numbers, in place.

    The mapping is learned from the readings themselves: any line that names both a known part
    and a supplier part number (a contract annex, a packing list) teaches one pair. Nothing is
    typed in by hand.
    """
    lines = [r for r in records if r["kind"] == "doc_line"]
    mapping = {
        line["attrs"]["supplier_part_no"]: line["material_id"]
        for line in lines
        if line["material_id"] in known_parts and line["attrs"]["supplier_part_no"]
    }
    for line in lines:
        material = line["material_id"]
        if material and material not in known_parts and material in mapping:
            line["material_id"] = mapping[material]
            line["attrs"]["mapped_from"] = material
        elif not material and line["attrs"]["supplier_part_no"] in mapping:
            line["material_id"] = mapping[line["attrs"]["supplier_part_no"]]
            line["attrs"]["mapped_from"] = line["attrs"]["supplier_part_no"]
